milestones.title: Mahim founded as the first town
milestones.detail: According to the Imperial Gazetteer no town existed on the islands until Raja Bhima founded Mahikavati (Mahim) after Ala-ud-din Khilji's raid into the Deccan in 1294; his followers settled across the island.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India, new edition (Oxford, 1908), vol. 8, p. 403, https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.207361

milestones.title: Islands conquered from Gujarat
milestones.detail: A Muslim force from Gujarat conquered Salsette and Bombay, ending Hindu rule; the islands stayed under Gujarat until 1534.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India, new edition (Oxford, 1908), vol. 8, p. 403, https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.207361

milestones.title: Treaty of Bassein: Portuguese rule
milestones.detail: Sultan Bahadur Shah of Gujarat ceded the seven islands of Bombay, with Bassein, to the Portuguese by the Treaty of Bassein of 23 December 1534.

milestones.title: Bombay ceded to the English Crown
milestones.detail: The islands passed to Charles II as part of Catherine of Braganza's dowry; Humphrey Cooke took possession in 1665.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India, new edition (Oxford, 1908), vol. 8, p. 404, https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.207361

milestones.title: Leased to the East India Company
milestones.detail: The Crown transferred the island to the East India Company. Gerald Aungier, governor from 1669 to 1677, is described as the real founder of the modern city.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India, new edition (Oxford, 1908), vol. 8, p. 404, https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.207361

milestones.title: Company headquarters moved from Surat
milestones.detail: The East India Company transferred its headquarters from Surat to Bombay.

milestones.title: Hornby Vellard joins the islands
milestones.detail: The Hornby Vellard causeway, begun in 1782 to unite Bombay's seven islands, was completed by 1784.

milestones.title: India's first passenger railway
milestones.detail: The first passenger railway in India opened between Bombay and Thana on 16 April 1853.

milestones.title: Fort walls demolished
milestones.detail: The walls of the Fort were demolished in 1862, making room for the public buildings facing Back Bay and other improvements.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India, new edition (Oxford, 1908), vol. 8, pp. 407-409, https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.207361

milestones.title: Suez Canal opens
milestones.detail: The opening of the Suez Canal made Bombay one of the largest seaports on the Arabian Sea.

milestones.title: Bubonic plague
milestones.detail: Plague broke out in August 1896 in the overcrowded quarters; the death rate of the city rose from 24 to 78 per 1,000 in the following years.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India, new edition (Oxford, 1908), vol. 8, pp. 410-412, https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.207361

milestones.title: Greater Bombay created
milestones.detail: In April 1950 the suburban and city districts were merged to create the Greater Bombay Municipal Corporation.

milestones.title: Capital of the new state of Maharashtra
milestones.detail: Bombay State was divided on linguistic lines on 1 May 1960 and Bombay became the capital of Maharashtra.

milestones.title: Bandra-Worli Sea Link
milestones.detail: The cable-stayed Bandra-Worli Sea Link across Mahim Bay was completed on 30 June 2009.

milestones.title: Mumbai Metro opens
milestones.detail: The first line of the Mumbai Metro began operation on 8 June 2014.

milestones.title: Trans Harbour Link to Navi Mumbai
milestones.detail: The 21.8 km Mumbai Trans Harbour Link, connecting Mumbai with Navi Mumbai, was inaugurated on 12 January 2024.

notes: Start date: contested, because Mumbai has no single founding. The islands were inhabited long before any town: Koli fishing communities, the Kanheri and other rock-cut caves in what are now the suburbs, and the Walkeshwar temple built under the Silahara chiefs (810-1260). The Imperial Gazetteer of 1908 states that no town sprang up until Raja Bhima founded Mahikavati (Mahim) following the raid of 1294; that is the start used here, marked estimated because the date comes from later chronicle tradition. The alternatives are 1534 (the Portuguese acquire the islands), 1661-68 (cession to the English Crown and transfer to the East India Company) or Aungier's governorship of 1669-77, which the Gazetteer calls the real founding of the modern city. The historic core given is Bombay Castle in the Fort, the nucleus of the English town; Mahim lies about 12 km to the north. Population: no figure was found for the period from 1294 to 1661. From 1661 to 1836 the points are travellers' and officials' estimates quoted in the Imperial Gazetteer, plus two of Chandler's figures; the 1780 figure is a rough count. The 1846 figure of 566,119 is doubtful (see its note). Censuses of 1864, 1872, 1881 and 1891 cover Bombay city and island. From 1901 to 1941 the points are the Census of India's back-series for the Greater Mumbai urban agglomeration (Table A-4, 2011), which fits the UN series from 1950; the like-for-like island figure for 1901 is 776,006, so part of the 1891-1901 change is a change of area. The 1901 census also fell during the plague, which had driven many residents away. Landmarks: skyscraper heights and completion years are from the CTBUH Skyscraper Center. Left out because no height was found on the pages opened: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (1888), the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel (1903), St Thomas Cathedral (1718), Haji Ali Dargah (1431) and Mount Mary Church. The Sea Link height is the 126 m quoted from The Times of India; the same Wikipedia article also gives 128 m. A milestone for Navi Mumbai was left out because the one founding date seen (1979, in the Wikipedia article on Mumbai) could not be cross-checked.
